faq.lead: Short, honest answers about what Masla-e-Karachi is and is not.
faq.what.a: It is an anonymous civic complaint and accountability platform for the people of Karachi. You report a problem with a photo and a location, the responsible department must answer, and departments are ranked on real data.
faq.live.a: Not yet. The real platform is under development. This website introduces the idea, and the button on every page takes you to the real website.
faq.political.q: Is it political or against the government?
faq.political.a: No. It is a non-political platform for everyone. It does not take sides and does not accuse any person.
faq.portal.q: Pakistan Citizen Portal already exists. What is different?
faq.portal.a: Masla-e-Karachi lets you complain anonymously, shows every problem on a public map, and ranks departments publicly on their results.
faq.force.q: Can it force a department to fix a problem?
faq.force.a: No. Its power is public transparency: everyone can see the problem, the reply and the result.
faq.name.q: Do I need to give my name?
faq.name.a: No. We never ask for your name, phone number or email, and you do not need to log in to report.
faq.find.q: Can anyone find out who reported a problem?
faq.find.a: We design the platform so that they cannot: photo details are removed, IP addresses are stored only as a hash, and every report is moderated. Read more on the privacy page.
faq.lost.q: What if I lose my tracking code?
faq.lost.a: It cannot be recovered, because we store only a scrambled version of it. Please keep it in a safe place.
faq.public.q: Are my photos shown to everyone?
faq.public.a: Photos are shown only after a moderator approves them, and faces and number plates are blurred. For sensitive problems the exact location and photo stay private.
faq.what-report.a: Civic problems such as open gutters, broken roads, garbage, water and sewerage, electricity, gas and street lights. Sensitive problems like illegal liquor dens, drug spots and bhatta (extortion) are handled with extra care.
faq.seven.q: How long does a department have to reply?
faq.seven.a: If nothing happens for 7 days, the problem is marked Overdue, a senior officer is emailed and the department’s ranking goes down.
faq.who-fixed.q: Who decides that a problem is fixed?
faq.who-fixed.a: The fix needs proof, an after-photo with a matching location. Then nearby residents confirm that it is really fixed.
faq.likes.a: No. Rankings use data only: resolution rate, average days, pending, overdue and reopened problems.
faq.abuse.q: How do I report abuse or ask for something to be removed?
faq.abuse.a: Use the contact details on this page and include the link to the report and what is wrong. Every report is reviewed by a moderator.
faq.emergency.a: No. If life is in danger, call 15 first. This website is not an emergency service.
faq.partner.q: I am a supporter, journalist or officer. How can I get in touch?
faq.partner.a: Please use the contact details on this page. We would be glad to hear from you.

problem.p: Most people see them, but very few complain. They fear their name will be exposed, they do not know which department to go to, and they rarely get a reply.
problem.gutter.p: A missing cover is a danger for every child, bike and car that passes by. Someone sees it, but no one reports it.
problem.road.p: Damaged roads slow everyone down and cause accidents, yet there is no simple way to say where and how bad.
problem.garbage.p: Piles that stay for days. Which department should clear them? Many residents do not know.
problem.water.p: Leaking pipes, overflowing sewers and water shortages.
problem.power.p: Dark streets, faulty lines and gas problems that go unreported.
problem.sensitive.p: Illegal liquor dens, drug spots and bhatta (extortion). Handled with extra care: the exact location and photo are never made public.
solution.p: Masla-e-Karachi turns a quiet complaint into a public record. The responsible department is named, its answer is visible, and the result is checked by the community.
solution.1.p: A photo or a video of up to 30 seconds, the location and a few details. No name, phone, email or login.
solution.2.p: After a moderator checks it, the problem appears on a public map and list that anyone can open.
solution.3.p: Every problem shows which department should fix it, such as KMC, KWSC, K-Electric or SSGC.
solution.4.p: Departments are ranked on how many problems they resolve and how fast. Likes are never used.
steps.1.p: Anyone reports a problem in four quick steps: category, location, photo or video, and details. A secret tracking code is given instead of an account.
steps.2.p: A moderator reviews every report before it goes public. Faces and number plates are blurred.
steps.3.p: The verified officer of the responsible department answers from an official dashboard. If nothing happens for 7 days, the problem is marked Overdue.
steps.4.p: The fix needs proof, an after-photo, and nearby residents confirm that it is really fixed.
feature.anon.p: We never ask for your name, phone number or email. Photo metadata is removed and your IP address is stored only as a hash.
feature.map.p: See what is wrong in your area and who is responsible, with Leaflet and OpenStreetMap.
feature.rank.p: Resolution rate, average days, pending, overdue and reopened. Public data, not opinions.
feature.stories.p: Problems that were really fixed, and the people and departments who did the work.
feature.status.p: Every report will show one clear status, so anyone can see where it stands.
depts.p: Each problem is linked to the department that should handle it. This list is for information. It does not say that any department is failing.
promise.p: You can report a problem without telling anyone who you are. Instead of an account you get a secret tracking code, and only a scrambled version of it is stored.

meta.privacy.title: Privacy and anonymity — Masla-e-Karachi
meta.privacy.desc: Your name is never taken. See how Masla-e-Karachi protects reporters: no personal details, photo metadata removed, hashed IP, moderation and private sensitive reports.
priv.lead: Anonymity is the core promise of Masla-e-Karachi. Here is what we do to protect you, in simple words.
priv.cmp.never.i4: A login or password to report
priv.ex.1.p1: Photos hide small details inside the file, such as the phone model, GPS and the time. Our server strips all of it before the photo is saved.
priv.v.exif: Removed by our server before anything is saved
priv.ex.2.h: A secret code, not an account
priv.ex.2.p1: After reporting you get a tracking code like the one shown. Use it to follow your report without ever creating an account.
priv.ex.2.p2: We keep only a scrambled version of the code. The trade-off: if you lose it, nobody can recover it for you.
priv.v.code: Example code. Only its hash is stored.
priv.ex.3.p1: To stop spam we need to notice when one connection sends many reports. We store only a scrambled hash of the IP address, never the address itself.
priv.v.ip: Turned into a scrambled hash (example address)
priv.ex.4.p1: A moderator checks each report before it goes public. Faces and number plates are blurred so that nobody is identified by accident.
priv.ex.5.p1: For problems like illegal liquor dens, drug spots and bhatta (extortion), the exact location and photo are not shown to the public. Only moderators and the relevant authority, such as the police or anti-narcotics, can see them.
priv.v.sens: Seen only by moderators and the relevant authority
priv.limits.h: About this website and our limits
priv.limits.p1: This landing website does not ask for or store any personal information, and it has no accounts. It does not use cookies or trackers.
priv.limits.p2: Fonts are served from our own server, so your browser does not contact Google or any other outside service to show them when a page opens.
priv.limits.p3: Anonymity also depends on what you share. Please avoid showing your own face, your house number or other details that could identify you in a photo or in the description.
priv.limits.p4: The real platform is still under development. Its full privacy policy will be finalised, with legal advice, before launch.

terms.about.p1: These terms explain how Masla-e-Karachi may be used and what may and may not be posted. By using the platform you agree to them.
terms.about.p2: Masla-e-Karachi is an independent, non-political platform. It is not a government service and it does not speak for any department.
terms.status.p1: The real platform is under development. This landing website only introduces the project. Features described here are planned and may change before launch.
terms.rules.intro: Please keep every report honest, respectful and about a civic problem.
terms.rules.yes.i1: A real problem you saw in Karachi
terms.rules.yes.i2: A clear photo or short video of the problem
terms.rules.yes.i3: The location and a few honest details
terms.rules.yes.i4: Facts: what you saw, where and when
terms.rules.no.i1: Names, phone numbers or addresses of people
terms.rules.no.i2: Accusations against a person, or political attacks
terms.rules.no.i3: Hate, threats, abuse or false reports
terms.rules.no.i4: Private photos, or faces you cannot blur
terms.moderation.p1: Every report is reviewed by a moderator before it becomes public. A moderator may edit, blur, hide or remove content that breaks these terms, is false or could put someone in danger.
terms.moderation.p2: If you believe something should be removed, contact us with the link and the reason. We will review it.
terms.anonymity.p1: You can report without giving your name, phone number or email. You stay responsible for what you post. Do not include details that identify you or other people.
terms.anonymity.p2: Your tracking code is the only way to follow your report. If you lose it, it cannot be recovered.
terms.departments.p1: Reports are statements by members of the public and have not been proved by us. Replies come from the verified officers of departments. We show what is submitted and do not guarantee that it is complete or correct.
terms.departments.p2: Rankings show public data about reports. They are not a verdict on any department or person.
terms.emergency.p1: If life is in danger, call 15 first. Do not use this website to ask for urgent help.
terms.content.p1: You keep the rights to the photos, videos and text you post. By posting, you allow Masla-e-Karachi to show them on the platform and to share them with the relevant department or authority so that the problem can be handled.
terms.liability.p1: We work to keep the platform safe and useful, but we cannot force any department to act and we do not promise that a problem will be fixed. The platform is provided as it is, to the extent allowed by law.
terms.law.p1: All content must follow the laws of Pakistan. These terms will be reviewed by a qualified lawyer before the real platform launches.
terms.changes.p1: We may update these terms as the platform grows. The date at the top of this page shows the latest version.
meta.how.title: How it works — Masla-e-Karachi
meta.how.desc: See how a problem goes from an anonymous report to a confirmed fix: moderation, department reply, community confirmation and public rankings.
how.lead: A simple look at what happens after someone reports a problem, step by step, in plain words.
callout.example.p: Ahmed is an imaginary person. His story shows how the platform is meant to work once it is live. The platform is still under development.
story.1.h: Ahmed sees an open gutter cover
story.1.p1: Ahmed is 32 and lives in Gulshan-e-Iqbal, Block 13-D. On his way home he sees a gutter with no cover.
story.1.p2: A neighbour shares the website link on WhatsApp. Ahmed reports the problem in four quick steps. He does not type his name, phone number or email.
story.1.p3: At the end he receives a secret tracking code to follow his report.
story.2.p1: A moderator reviews the photo and the location. Faces and number plates are blurred.
story.2.p2: Once approved, the problem appears on the public map as a red pin, with the responsible department named: KWSC.
story.3.p1: Neighbours open the report and press “I am affected too”. The verified KWSC officer answers from the official dashboard, fixes the gutter and uploads an after-photo.
story.3.p2: Everyone can see that the department responded.
story.4.p1: Residents nearby are asked if it is really fixed. They confirm, and the pin turns green.
story.4.p2: The story appears in Success Stories, and the department’s record improves because the fix is real.
form.p: No account. No name. It is made to work on a phone.
form.1.p: Choose what kind of problem it is: gutter, road, garbage, water, electricity, gas and more.
form.2.p: Use your phone’s GPS or place a pin on the map.
form.3.p: Add a photo or a video of up to 30 seconds.
form.4.p: Say a few words about what is wrong.
legend.p: Only four colours, always used in the same way.
legend.open: The problem is public and is waiting for the department.
legend.review: A moderator is checking the report before it goes public.
legend.responded: The department has replied and work is going on.
legend.resolved: It is fixed, with proof, and the community has confirmed it.
acc.p: Three simple rules keep the system fair.
acc.1.p1: If a department does nothing for 7 days, the problem gets an Overdue flag.
acc.1.p2: A senior officer is emailed and the department’s ranking goes down. Everyone can see it.
acc.2.p1: Sometimes a neighbour fixes the problem. Any user can press “This Problem Is Fixed” and upload an after-photo.
acc.2.p2: The photo’s location must match the original. A moderator checks it, nearby residents vote, and then it is marked as resolved by the community. Department rankings only count work the department really did.
acc.3.p1: Departments are ranked on what they actually did. Popularity and likes are never part of the ranking.
cmp.h: What we do and what we do not
cmp.p: We are honest about our limits.
cmp.do.i1: Let anyone report without giving a name
cmp.do.i2: Make every problem and every reply public
cmp.do.i4: Ask the community to confirm fixes
cmp.never.i1: Force a department to act: our power is public transparency
cmp.never.i2: Take sides in politics or accuse any person
cmp.never.i3: Ask for your name, phone number or email
